To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decay-energy distribution from neutron knockout of 12 Be to 11 Be is consistent with the existence of a single 80(2)-keV state in 11 Be.

the data from the neutron knockout reaction of 12 B e at 70 A · MeV are well described with the decay of a single resonance at a decay energy of 80(2 ) keV, with the 2 + 10 Be state in the final state.

the data from the 12 Be(d,p)13 Be experiment at 40 MeV can be described with a single resonance decaying to the excited 2 + state of 10 Be with a decay energy of 80 keV and that a fit of the data with a contribution of an 86-ke V decay-energy channel from the 3.955-MeV state in 11 Be is not consistent with the data. In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 11 Be data presented in our original paper are consistent with a single resonance decaying to the ground state of 10 Be.
the data cannot be described with two decay channels as suggested by Fortune, but can be described with a single decay channel.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data from the original paper [2] can be described with a single resonance with a decay energy of 80(2 keV) decaying to the first excited 2 + state of 10 Be, with a reduced-χ2 value of 0.8.

we have measured the 12 Be (p, p′) reaction at a proton energy of 200 MeV and observed a resonance in the neutron-unbound 11 Be spectrum at 80(4) keV, which is in good agreement with a previous measurement [2].

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the 2 + resonance in 10 Be is fed by a single neutron-unbound state in 11 Be with a decay energy of 80(2 keV).
the 3.955-MeV state is not populated in the 11 Be knockout process.
the decay-energy distribution of 11 Be is consistent with a single resonance.
